messages:
liz: FYI seeing trace holes for tenant=redwood-beta after the header-sanitize canary rolled at ~09:11 UTC. traces arrive but child segments missing. first noticed at 09:12 and persisted for ~30-40m.
sam: gaps = missing child spans (e.g. svcA -> (gap) -> svcC) or missing parents?
liz: child spans specifically. parent ids present in the root.
priya: also seeing a spike in exporter errors at the same time — 502s and flush broken pipe logs. attaching snippets.
priya: ```2026-03-17T09:13:02Z exporter[pid=1234] WARN export failed status=502 body="upstream protocol error"
2026-03-17T09:13:03Z exporter[pid=1234] ERROR flush failed: broken pipe```
sam: the canary changed router header sanitizer to trim headers >128 chars. it was supposed to drop control chars only, not truncate tracestate.
jon: truncating tracestate seems suspicious. if the header gets cut mid-value some HTTP layers treat it as malformed. any packet captures?
liz: tcpdump shows traceparent present until router, but router->backend requests have tracestate shortened/truncated around 120 chars. snippet:
```=> GET /api/foo HTTP/1.1
=> traceparent: 00-4bf92f...-01
=> tracestate: vendor1=longkv...,vendor2=othervalues,truncatED=<<<```
mica: collector side accepts traceparent + tracestate as opaque headers; truncation alone shouldn't drop spans unless parent id changed or upstream returned 400.
priya: exporter 502s spike lines up exactly with canary percentage increase. ingress latency doesn't change, suggesting header sanitization caused upstream rejections.
sam: could sanitizer be inserting invalid bytes or leaving partial CRLF? nginx often returns 400 or drops headers for invalid header syntax.
liz: I reproduced locally: curling with a very long tracestate to router path returns 400 and router drops the header and closes connection.
liz: ```$ curl -v -H "traceparent: 00-...-...-01" -H "tracestate: vendor=aaaaaaaaaaa..."
< HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
< Connection: close```
deploy-bot: canary rollout router/header-sanitize v2 -> 10% nodes @2026-03-17T09:11:00Z
sam: rolling back canary now to verify correlation
deploy-bot: rollback router/header-sanitize v2 -> 0% nodes @2026-03-17T09:48:12Z
priya: after rollback exporter 502s went back to baseline and new traces no longer show missing child spans.
liz: confirmed — at 09:55 traces for same tenant include the expected child segments.
mica: preliminary root cause: sanitizer truncated long tracestate entries instead of stripping only invalid control chars. truncated tracestate led to malformed header observed by upstream -> requests rejected -> agent/collector didn't get downstream spans.
sam: action items: 1) revert behavior in sanitizer so it drops header if unsafe instead of truncating; 2) add unit + e2e tests for tracestate edge cases (long, commas, unicode, control chars); 3) add alerting: exporter 5xx burst + trace-gap metric.
jon: I'll open a PR with the sanitizer fix and tests, assigning to @sam for review.
liz: i'll draft a brief incident note in incidents/ and add timeline and tcpdump excerpts. thanks all. :thumbsup:
